visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a young woman standing outdoors in front of a small, yellow-painted building with a distinctive pointed roof featuring an acorn logo. She wears a black beanie and a black jacket with white ruffles, gesturing toward the shop entrance while a red brick wall is visible to the left. (2) Inside the shop, the camera focuses on a wooden counter where a menu board is displayed, showing pricing options for caricatures in Traditional Chinese and Korean. A hand with manicured nails points at the text, while a wooden shelf behind the counter displays various small art samples and decorative items. (3) The scene shifts to a wall covered in black-and-white comic-strip style caricatures, some featuring pets like dogs and cats. The woman's hand reaches out to touch one of the strips, highlighting the variety of illustration styles available in the studio. (4) The woman is now seated at a drawing station across from a female artist wearing a tan beret and a face mask. Numerous drawing samples are arranged on the desk between them, and the artist begins to sketch on a vertical paper strip. (5) A sequence of shots shows the woman posing with various cheerful expressions—winking, smiling, and making peace signs—as the artist works. The lighting is warm and indoor, focusing on the interaction between the subject and the creator. (6) The completed caricature is revealed: a four-frame vertical strip in a comic style, packaged in a brown envelope with decorative stickers. The woman holds it up to the camera, smiling broadly to show her satisfaction with the final artwork. (7) The woman walks toward a second shop location with a glass-fronted entrance adorned with many portrait samples. Inside, she sits for another drawing, this time for a single-frame portrait, and the video concludes with a side-by-side comparison of the two different illustration results.
